summary: Extended the partition experiment with a healing phase and registered it as a successor. The harness now reconnects the two sides after both have led and committed, waits twice the election window, and reports how many leaders remain and whether each side's committed entry still exists. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the cluster converged to a single leader but both divergent committed entries were still present, each on its own side, which the source explains because AppendEntries matches stored entries by index and term only while the two same-term leaders wrote different content at the same index, so each side treats the other's entry as a duplicate and never truncates it; with the flag disabled only the one committed entry survives. Three comparisons are declared (convergence to one leader for the flagged case, exactly one surviving divergent entry for the flagged case, and the control). Validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so this observation is not yet part of the account, and I have deliberately not claimed anything about state-machine contents or about reconciliation by an operator — only the presence of the two payloads in the log stores, which the next interpretation will confirm or correct against the receipt.
